newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Leisurenet says in talks on food interests.
newsitem.headline: Leisurenet says in talks on food interests.

text.p: South African health, education and foods group, Leisurenet Ltd, said on Wednesday it was in talks on the possible sale of its food interests.
The group gave no further details in a brief statement, other than to advise shareholders to exercise caution in their sharedealings.

The announcement follows a report in a local newspaper on Wednesday that the firm was planning to sell off its food franchising interests in a bid to sharpen focus on its core health and fitness divisions.
Business Report, quoting a market source, said a Malaysian-backed firm, NKH, was interested in the group's Foodgro division. The source estimated that Foodgro could fetch over 120 million rand.
Mico Smuts, Leisurenet commercial director, declined to comment. "We cannot comment at all as it is under a cautionary," he told Reuters.

Foodgro, whose interests include franchising operations Black Steer, Macrib and Bulldogs Pubs, in December secured the rights to U.S. restaurant chain Planet Hollywood International. The first outlet will be opened this year.
Leisurenet last year blazed an acquisition trail through the education sector, snapping up a stake in private schools group Crawford Education Holdings and buying Varsity College.
It also purchased golfing chain the Pro Shop in December.
At 0825 GMT Leisurenet shares on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange were trading 15 cents or 3.5 percent stronger at 430 cents in volume of 273,800 shares.
